newsitem.title: USA: First lady drops in at MTV party.
newsitem.headline: First lady drops in at MTV party.

text.p: First lady Hillary Clinton dropped in at the Conde Nast-MTV pre-inaugural bash Saturday and thanked everyone for their support.
"I hope you're all having a great time," she said emerging from a VIP room closed to most of the partygoers at the Corcoran Gallery.

"I just thought I'd come by and say thank you all very, very much," Clinton, dressed in a sparkly dark jacket, said as she waved to the crowd at one of several parties being held on the opening night of inauguration weekend.

President Clinton, who will be inaugurated to a second term Monday, was not with her, and while daughter Chelsea was on the guest list, she was not spotted. At least one of Vice President Al Gore's daughters attended.

Actors, including Kevin Spacey and Ron Silver, models such as Beverly Johnson, and comedians including Conan O'Brien mixed with politicians and other guests from the music, publishing and fashion industries.
Politicians who attended expressed sadness at the death of former Massachusetts senator and Democratic presidential candidate Paul Tsongas.

Tsongas retired from Congress in 1985 to battle a deadly form of bone cancer and ran for president in 1992, losing the Democratic presidential nomination to Clinton. Tsongas died of pneumonia Saturday.

"Here's this guy who is living in great pain, living under a death sentence and never stopped to feel self pity," Representative Barney Frank, D-Mass., said as he arrived for the party. "I think that really is the best way to remember him."
Inside the gallery was packed with people. The artwork had been removed from the walls or enclosed in closed-off areas.
Martinis in a rainbow of colours, including bright blue and red, were the speciality drinks, while crab cakes, sushi and quiche were set out for nibbling. Everyone working wore black.
Miss America Tara Holland showed up in a short black and leopard print dress. There were more mink coats than tuxedos at the non-black tie event.
Cabinet members stopping in included Health and Human Services Secretary Donna Shalala.
"I like parties, what do you think the cabinet is dull?" she joked. "This is supposed to be the party of the year."
